studies.title: Understanding social dysfunction in the behavioural variant of frontotemporal dementia: the role of emotion and sarcasm processing.
studies.abstract: Social interaction is profoundly affected in the behavioural form of frontotemporal dementia (bvFTD) yet there are few means of objectively assessing this. Diagnosis of bvFTD is based on informant report, however a number of individuals with a clinical profile consistent with the disease have no imaging abnormality and seem to remain stable, with doubt about the presence of underlying neurodegenerative pathology. We aimed to quantify aspects of the behavioural disorder and link it to the underlying level of atrophy in socially relevant brain regions. We tested individuals with either bvFTD (N = 26) or Alzheimer's disease (N = 9) and 16 controls using The Awareness of Social Inference Test (TASIT) to assess their ability to identify emotion and sarcasm in video vignettes. A subset of bvFTD patients (N = 21) and controls (N = 12) were scanned using MRI within 6 months of assessment. There was marked impairment in the ability of bvFTD patients whose scans showed abnormalities to recognize sarcastic, but not sincere statements. Their capacity to interpret negative emotion was also impaired, and this appeared to be a major factor underlying the deficit in sarcasm recognition. Clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients whose scans were normal, Alzheimer's disease patients and controls had no difficulty in appreciating both types of statement. In a multivariate imaging analysis it was shown that the sarcasm (and emotion recognition) deficit was dependent on a circuit involving the lateral orbitofrontal cortex, insula, amygdala and temporal pole, particularly on the right. Performance on a more global test of cognitive function, the Addenbrooke's Cognitive Examination did not have a unique association with these regions. The TASIT is an objective test of social dysfunction in bvFTD which indexes the frontotemporal volume loss in bvFTD patients and provides an objective measure for separating behavioural patients who are likely to decline from those who may remain stable. These results provide additional evidence for the role of the orbitofrontal cortex and related structures in the processing of socially relevant signals, particularly those where negative emotion recognition is important.

studies.title: Functional MRI of music emotion processing in frontotemporal dementia.
studies.abstract: Frontotemporal dementia is an important neurodegenerative disorder of younger life led by profound emotional and social dysfunction. Here we used fMRI to assess brain mechanisms of music emotion processing in a cohort of patients with frontotemporal dementia (n = 15) in relation to healthy age-matched individuals (n = 11). In a passive-listening paradigm, we manipulated levels of emotion processing in simple arpeggio chords (mode versus dissonance) and emotion modality (music versus human emotional vocalizations). A complex profile of disease-associated functional alterations was identified with separable signatures of musical mode, emotion level, and emotion modality within a common, distributed brain network, including posterior and anterior superior temporal and inferior frontal cortices and dorsal brainstem effector nuclei. Separable functional signatures were identified post-hoc in patients with and without abnormal craving for music (musicophilia): a model for specific abnormal emotional behaviors in frontotemporal dementia. Our findings indicate the potential of music to delineate neural mechanisms of altered emotion processing in dementias, with implications for future disease tracking and therapeutic strategies.

This study includes FDG-PET (I3), includes clinically diagnosed behavioural variant FTD patients (I4) with adequate sample sizes (20 FTD patients; controls n=38) satisfying I5. Therefore it does not meet I6 and I7 (no group-level voxelwise contrast or whole-brain results for the target sample). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). No exclusion criteria were triggered.

This study is excluded because it does not provide bvFTD-specific whole-brain voxelwise results with an adequate bvFTD sample. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (uses resting-state fMRI) and I4 (included clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients). Inclusion criteria NOT met: I5 (bvFTD subgroup N=4, which is <6 required), I6 (no reported between-group contrast specifically comparing a bvFTD-only group to controls—the paper reports an aggregated FTD group and discusses FTD subtypes pooled), and I7 (no whole-brain, group-level voxelwise result clearly identified as coming from the bvFTD target sample alone). No exclusion criteria from the provided list apply. The full text appears complete. Because the meta-analysis objective specifically targets bvFTD and requires bvFTD-specific, whole-brain contrasts with sufficient sample size, this study must be excluded.

This empirical study used voxel-based morphometry (VBM) on 3T MRI and reports voxelwise group analyses. The sample includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (n=19) and healthy controls (n=20), meeting minimum sample-size requirements. The paper reports between-group voxelwise contrasts comparing patient groups (bvFTD and SD) to controls (voxel-wise two-sample t-tests) with results referenced to MNI space and statistical parametric maps/tables presented. Whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results for the bvFTD group versus controls are reported (atrophy maps and VBM behavioural correlates). No exclusion criteria apply (not a review, not ROI-only, not DTI/FC-only, and patient sample appears free of excluded comorbidities). Full text appears complete with methods, results, and discussion. Therefore the study meets the review’s inclusion criteria for bvFTD neuroimaging VBM studies.

(a) Exclusion criteria met: none. (b) Inclusion criteria met: I3 (study used VBM), I4 (cohort includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients, n=22), I5 (patient group and healthy control group sizes >=6). (c) Inclusion criteria not met: I6 and I7. The paper does not report any between-group whole-brain (voxelwise) contrast that isolates the bvFTD group versus healthy controls in stereotactic (MNI/Talairach) coordinates. VBM analyses reported are symptom-correlations within the combined FTLD cohort (and within the AD cohort) and regressions including syndromic group as a covariate, rather than a bvFTD vs control group-level voxelwise contrast. No bvFTD-specific whole-brain coordinate-based results are provided in the text or tables; therefore the study does not satisfy the requirement for bvFTD-specific whole-brain between-group results. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

The full-text is complete and reports an empirical imaging study of clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=82) and healthy controls (n=80). Voxel-based morphometry (VBM) preprocessing and whole-brain SPM12 voxel-wise group comparisons are described, including normalization to MNI space and voxelwise results (with cluster thresholds and correction). The paper reports between-group contrasts (bvFTD vs controls) and stage-specific whole-brain voxelwise results, satisfying whole-brain, coordinate-based reporting requirements. No exclusion criteria are met (not a review/meta-analysis; not ROI-only; not non-empirical; sample exclusions for comorbidities are appropriate). Therefore the study meets all required inclusion criteria for the review.

Excluded because the imaging modality is surface-based cortical thickness analysis of structural MRI rather than VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET — this fails inclusion criterion I3 and meets exclusion criterion E9 (cortical thickness-only study). The study does meet I4 (clinically diagnosed bvFTD sample) and I5 (sample sizes: 88 bvFTD, 30 controls). It also provides whole-brain vertex-wise analyses (satisfying I7) and reports results in figures/supplementary materials (I8). However, it does not report between-group results in stereotaxic coordinates (MNI/Talairach), so I6 is not met. Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false).

Exclusion (E6) applies: the study performs ROI-based network analyses using AAL parcellation and MST on regionwise wavelet correlation matrices; it does not report voxelwise, whole-brain group-level results in a stereotactic coordinate space (MNI/Talairach). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (resting-state fMRI used), I4 (clinically diagnosed bvFTD sample), I5 (n=41 bvFTD, n=39 controls). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 and I7 (no between-group voxelwise contrasts reported in MNI/Talairach coordinates; results are region/ROI-level and graph-based rather than whole-brain voxelwise statistical maps). Full text appears complete; decision based on methods and results sections describing ROI-based analyses without coordinate tables or voxelwise group contrasts.

The full text demonstrates all required inclusion criteria: imaging modality is VBM (I3); includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=23) (I4); sample sizes meet thresholds for patient and control groups (bvFTD n=23; controls n=16) (I5); reports between-group voxelwise VBM contrasts in MNI standard space comparing bvFTD to controls (I6), with group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) results presented and described (FWE-corrected, p<0.05) (I7); results are presented in figures and text (I8). The article is an empirical study with complete core sections (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion). No exclusion criteria are met (not a review/meta-analysis, not ROI-only, not solely other modalities). Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false).

Although this study uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) and includes a large cohort with clinically diagnosed behavioural variant FTD (bvFTD) and Pick’s disease cases, the voxelwise, whole-brain VBM results reported are organized by pathological groups (e.g., TDP-C, Pick’s, MAPT mutations, etc.), not by the clinical bvFTD syndromic group. The review inclusion requires at least one group-level, whole-brain voxelwise contrast in standard space comparing a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (not pooled with other patient groups) to healthy controls. This study does not present such bvFTD-vs-control voxelwise coordinates or maps (MNI/Talairach) for the clinical bvFTD group, so it fails inclusion criteria I6 and I7. Full text appears complete.

This is a genetic/clinical case series of TBK1 mutation carriers that includes several patients with behavioural-variant FTD and used FDG-PET in two patients (so I3, I4, and I5 are met: FDG-PET modality present; study includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients; there are ≥6 FTD patients in the cohort). However, the paper does not report any group-level between-group voxelwise contrasts in a standard stereotaxic space (MNI/Talairach) comparing a bvFTD group to healthy controls, nor any whole-brain, voxelwise group results or coordinate tables/figures suitable for meta-analysis. Therefore it fails I6 and I7. Because no whole-brain group results are provided, it falls under the exclusion of studies without whole-brain results (E6). Full text appears complete.

Exclusion decision because the study is a small case series and does not provide group-level, whole-brain neuroimaging contrasts required for the meta-analysis. Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: I3 (uses FDG‑PET in several cases) and I4 (includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD cases). Inclusion IDs not met: I5 (fewer than 6 patients in the bvFTD/patient group; only five symptomatic cases), I6 (no between‑group voxelwise contrast comparing bvFTD group to controls in MNI/Talairach space), I7 (no group‑level whole‑brain voxelwise results clearly identified as coming from the target sample). Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false).

Full text is complete. This fMRI resting-state study includes clinically diagnosed FTD patients (including 18 bvFTD cases) and reports whole-brain voxelwise ICA results correlating Reserve Index with functional connectivity. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (resting-state fMRI), I4 (sample includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD cases), I5 (patient subgroup size ≥6), I8 (results reported with MNI coordinates/voxelwise clusters). However, it does NOT meet I6: the paper does not report any between-group contrast comparing a bvFTD group to healthy controls (bvFTD results are not presented as a distinct between-group contrast against controls). Consequently I7 is not met for the target comparison: there are no group-level, whole-brain voxelwise results clearly identified as coming from a bvFTD vs control contrast. Because both I6 and I7 are required, the study must be excluded.

Study meets several inclusion criteria: it used FDG-PET (I3), included clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=90) (I4), and has sufficient sample sizes (I5). However, the full text does not provide a clear between-group, whole-brain (voxelwise) contrast reported in a defined stereotactic space (MNI or Talairach) for the bvFTD group versus controls. Although preprocessing used MNI normalization and voxelwise SPM analyses were performed for the overall FTLD group, the manuscript does not present coordinates or an explicit group-level voxelwise contrast for bvFTD (I6 and I7 not satisfied). Therefore it cannot be included for coordinate-based meta-analysis.

The provided full text is a corrigendum (funding correction) only and does not include core article content (introduction, methods, results). Therefore I cannot verify any required inclusion criteria. Specifically: inclusion criteria not met/uncertain - I3 (imaging modality: VBM/fMRI/FDG-PET) not reported; I4 (clinically diagnosed bvFTD/Pick's disease sample) not confirmed; I5 (sample sizes ≥6) not reported; I6 (between-group MNI/Talairach coordinates for bvFTD vs controls) not reported; I7 (whole-brain voxelwise group-level result) not reported; I8 (format of whole-brain results) not verifiable. Exclusion criteria met: E8 (the provided document is a non-empirical corrigendum without original data). Because the full text is incomplete (corrigendum only), the study cannot be assessed against the review criteria and is excluded.

This is an empirical, whole-brain, voxel-wise longitudinal MRI study of frontotemporal lobar degeneration that includes a distinct bvFTD group (n=44) and controls (n=97). The methods use voxel-wise gray-matter contraction/expansion maps computed with SPM12 and DARTEL, normalized to MNI space, and report between-group t-maps and consensus voxelwise ROIs comparing bvFTD to controls. Sample sizes exceed the minimum. Whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results for bvFTD versus controls are presented (figures, maps, and effect sizes). No exclusion criteria (e.g., review-only, ROI-only, seed-based FC/DTI/cortical-thickness-only) apply. Full text (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion) is provided. Therefore all required inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6, I7, I8) are met and no exclusion criteria are triggered.

This is an original empirical study that uses VBM (PELICAN/VBM) alongside DBM and FreeSurfer metrics, includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD subgroup (n=77) and healthy controls (n=136), and reports group-level, whole-brain voxel-wise comparisons between bvFTD and controls in standard template space (analyses registered to MNI152; voxel-/vertex-wise results and regional results are provided and downloadable). Sample sizes exceed the minimum (≥6) for patient and control groups. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, and provides whole-brain voxelwise findings clearly attributed to bvFTD versus controls. No exclusion criteria are met (not a review, not ROI-only, not non-empirical, and does not rely solely on excluded modalities). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and should be included.

This is an empirical study that used FDG-PET (and ASL-MRI) and included a clearly clinically diagnosed bvFTD sample (n=32) with cognitively normal controls (n=15). The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise group comparisons (GLM and PLS logistic regression) with images normalized to a template and presents group-level voxelwise results contrasting bvFTD vs. controls and bvFTD vs. AD (figures and voxelwise analyses). The sample sizes exceed the minimum, and results are presented as whole-brain voxelwise maps (figures and statistical parametric maps) suitable for inclusion. Full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so the record appears complete.

This study used DTI tractography and a targeted VBM approach applied to an anterior cingulate mask rather than reporting whole-brain, voxelwise group comparisons in stereotactic space with coordinates. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (uses VBM method—FSL-VBM modification applied), I4 (clinically diagnosed bvFTD sample), I5 (≥6 patients and ≥6 controls). Inclusion criteria NOT met: I6 (no reported between-group contrast results in defined stereotactic space with coordinates/MNI or Talairach reported), I7 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise results—analyses were ROI/masked to the ACC and tract-specific). Exclusion criteria applied: E6 (study reports only ROI/tract-based analyses with no whole-brain voxelwise results). Full text appears complete (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion). Therefore excluded for failing whole-brain/voxelwise reporting requirements.

This is an empirical VBM study in PLOS ONE that includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (n=18) and healthy controls (n=27). It uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) as the imaging modality and reports whole-brain, voxelwise between-group contrasts (bvFTD vs controls) with MNI stereotaxic coordinates and figures; analyses were performed separately for bvFTD (not pooled with other FTD subtypes). The study also provides group-level whole-brain results (FWE-corrected atrophy maps and uncorrected voxelwise correlations reported with cluster extent) and presents coordinates in text/figures. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, and no exclusion criteria (e.g., review/meta-analysis, ROI-only, DTI/FC-only methods, or samples with disqualifying comorbidities) are violated. Full text appears complete.

Although this study used VBM and FDG-PET and reports whole-brain voxelwise group analyses, it is excluded because it does not provide bvFTD-specific between-group contrasts. The FTLD patient sample (n=11) is a mixed group (FTD n=4, semantic dementia n=5, mixed n=2) and results are reported for the pooled FTLD group versus controls rather than for a clinically defined bvFTD (behavioral-variant FTD) subgroup. Therefore: (a) I6 is not satisfied (no between-group contrast specifically for bvFTD vs. controls in stereotactic coordinates); (b) I4 is not satisfied (bvFTD diagnosis is not clearly isolated/present as a target sample); (c) I5 is not satisfied for a bvFTD subgroup because the FTD subgroup has only 4 patients (<6). Inclusion criteria satisfied: I3 (VBM/FDG-PET used), I7 (whole-brain voxelwise results reported), I8 (results clearly described in text/figures). No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) applied. Full text appears complete.

The study reports VBM and DTI analyses in clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients and controls with MNI coordinates provided (I3, I4, I5, I6 satisfied). However, the imaging analyses were conducted using an ROI mask confined to predefined motor-system regions rather than reporting whole-brain, voxelwise group-level results. Therefore it does not provide whole-brain voxelwise results from the target sample (I7 not met) and meets exclusion criterion E6 (ROI-only analyses with no whole-brain results). Full text appears complete.

This study meets all inclusion criteria: I3 - uses FDG-PET (and early-phase florbetapir pseudo-FDG); I4 - includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=8); I5 - patient group size ≥6 (bvFTD n=8) and control group size ≥6 (CN n=10); I6 - reports between-group voxelwise SPM contrasts comparing bvFTD to controls (two-sample t-tests in SPM12, results in stereotactic space); I7 - provides group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) results (SPM and BPM voxelwise analyses, figures and descriptions); I8 - whole-brain results presented in figures and described in text. No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) are met. Full text appears complete (contains Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, Conclusions).

Although the study includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=84) and uses whole-brain VBM (I3, I4, I5 satisfied) and reports voxelwise results/coordinates (I8 satisfied), it does not report any between-group contrast comparing a bvFTD group to healthy controls (no control group or bvFTD-vs-control voxelwise contrast). Therefore it fails inclusion criteria I6 (bvFTD vs controls contrast) and I7 (whole-brain voxelwise result originating from the bvFTD vs control comparison). Full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria from the list are triggered.

Study uses FDG-PET (I3 satisfied). However it does not provide data specific to clinically diagnosed behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD) or Pick's disease: the FTLD group includes 13 patients with only 3 labelled as 'FTD' (not specified as bvFTD), so there is no distinct bvFTD group (I4 not met). The bvFTD-relevant subgroup size is <6 (FTD n=3), so the sample-size criterion for the target group is not met (I5 not met). The reported between-group voxelwise contrasts are for aggregated FTLD (vs subjective cognitive impairment) rather than a bvFTD group unpooled from other diagnoses, so there is no between-group contrast specific to bvFTD (I6 not met) and no whole-brain result clearly identified as coming from a bvFTD sample (I7 not met). No exclusion criteria were triggered. Full text appears complete.

This study includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients and uses resting-state fMRI and DTI (I3,I4) with adequate sample sizes (bvFTD n=12; controls n=18) (I5). However, it does not report any whole-brain, voxelwise group-level results in a standard stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach): diffusion results are tract-specific (DTI/tractography) and functional results are ROI-to-ROI DMN connectivity (ROI-based) with non-significant between-group voxelwise findings. Therefore it fails to meet I6 and I7 (no between-group voxelwise coordinates/whole-brain maps for bvFTD vs controls). Because the paper reports only tract-based DTI and ROI/seed-based functional connectivity (no voxelwise VBM/fMRI/FDG-PET coordinate results), it meets exclusion criteria E6 (only ROI analyses / no whole-brain results) and E9 (reports DTI and seed/ROI FC rather than whole-brain voxelwise modalities required). Full text appears complete. Exclusion based on E6 and E9.

This is an empirical VBM study of clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (23 patients included) with a healthy control group (20 controls). The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise VBM group comparisons (two-sample t-test) showing atrophic clusters in bilateral anterior temporal lobes and additional regions, and voxelwise regression analyses relating behavioral measures to GM volume in the patient group. Imaging modality includes VBM (and FDG-PET performed in most patients). Sample sizes exceed the minimum (patients=23, controls=20). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise results comparing bvFTD to controls are reported. Full text contains Introduction, Methods (including VBM preprocessing and statistics), Results (behavior and imaging) and Discussion; core article content is present. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, I7 and the reporting allowance I8. No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) apply. Full text appears complete.

This study includes FDG-PET imaging and reports whole-brain voxel-wise group differences for an FTD group (n=62) and specifies 48 bvFTD and 14 svPPA within that group. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (FDG-PET used), I4 (bvFTD patients included in sample), I5 (bvFTD subgroup n=48 and controls n=73 exceed n>=6), I8 (whole-brain results reported in figures/text). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no reported between-group voxelwise contrast results shown specifically for the bvFTD subgroup separate from other FTD variants), I7 (whole-brain results are reported for the combined FTD group rather than clearly identified as coming from the bvFTD target sample). No exclusion criteria were triggered. Therefore the paper must be excluded for the review because the target group (bvFTD) is not analyzed/presented separately in whole-brain between-group contrasts.

This study is excluded because it does not provide the required whole-brain, voxelwise group-level results comparing a clearly identified bvFTD (behavioral-variant FTD) group to controls in stereotactic space. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (FDG-PET was used) and I5 (patient group size for FTD = 17, which is ≥6). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (paper reports ‘FTD’ but does not explicitly state clinically diagnosed behavioral-variant FTD or Pick’s disease), I6 (no between-group contrast results reported as coordinates in MNI/Talairach comparing bvFTD to controls), I7 (no clearly reported whole-brain, voxelwise group-level result from the target sample), and I8 (no coordinate tables/figures of whole-brain results for bvFTD). Exclusion criteria applied: E6 (the study presents diagnostic accuracy and region/volume-of-interest/3D-SSP descriptions without reporting whole-brain voxelwise coordinate results). Full text appears complete (background, methods, results, discussion).

This study reports voxel-based morphometry (VBM) analyses with whole-brain, cluster-corrected results (p < .05 FWE) and presents atrophy patterns for patient groups including a standalone bvFTD group (n=18) and healthy controls (n=37). It uses VBM as the imaging modality (I3), includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (I4) and sufficient sample sizes (I5). The manuscript reports whole-brain voxelwise analyses and brain–behavior correlations and references group-level atrophy maps for each patient group; these constitute between-group voxelwise contrasts and whole-brain results attributable to the bvFTD sample (I6, I7). Results are presented in figures/tables and described in the text (I8). No exclusion criteria are met: this is an empirical study (not a review), it reports whole-brain VBM (not ROI-only), does not rely solely on seed-based FC/DTI/cortical thickness, and does not indicate disqualifying comorbid samples. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore, it meets all required inclusion criteria and should be included in the review.

The full text reports resting-state fMRI (rs-fMRI) and diffusion MRI analyses; rs-fMRI (ICA/dual-regression of the DMN) satisfies imaging modality criterion (I3). The sample includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=12) and controls (n=17), meeting I4 and I5 (both groups ≥6). The manuscript reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise between-group contrasts (Randomise, one-way ANCOVA and post-hoc t-tests) for DMN connectivity and TBSS-based DTI metrics; results are reported as cluster-based whole-brain findings with reference to supplement tables (acceptable per I6 and I8). Whole-brain voxelwise evidence from the target bvFTD group is clearly presented (I7). No exclusion criteria apply: this is an empirical study (not a review), reports whole-brain analyses (not ROI-only), and does not ONLY report seed-based FC, DTI, or cortical thickness (it includes whole-brain rs-fMRI ICA results). Full text appears complete. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and none of the exclusion criteria.

This empirical study includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (n=41) and a matched control group (n=100), uses voxelwise structural MRI (VBM-derived W-scores in MNI152 space) and resting-state fMRI, and reports syndrome-specific, group-level whole-brain results comparing each syndrome (including bvFTD) to cognitively normal controls. At least one between-group contrast for bvFTD versus controls is presented (syndrome – cognitively normal whole-brain atrophy/FC maps and reconstructed FC matrices), and figures and voxelwise analyses are reported in MNI space. Sample sizes exceed the minimum of 6 per group. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion and appears complete. No exclusion criteria (reviews, ROI-only, non-empirical, or disallowed modalities) apply. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8 and is suitable for inclusion.

This study includes resting-state fMRI (I3), clinically diagnosed bvFTD cases (n=35) (I4), and sufficient sample sizes for patients and controls (I5). However, it does not report voxelwise whole-brain results in a standard stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach). Analyses are connectome/parcellation-based (220 regions) using network-based statistics and single-subject connectome distributions rather than voxelwise group-level contrasts with coordinates. Therefore inclusion criteria I6 (between-group contrasts reported in MNI/Talairach) and I7 (at least one group-level whole-brain voxelwise result from the target bvFTD sample) are not met. This meets exclusion E6 (studies reporting only ROI/parcellation-based analyses with no whole-brain voxelwise results). Full text appears complete. Consequently the article is excluded from the meta-analysis.

Although this empirical study uses FDG-PET (I3) and includes a substantial number of participants with a predominant behavioral phenotype (bvFTD) meeting the sample-size requirement (I4, I5), it does not report any between-group, whole-brain voxelwise contrasts in a standard stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach) comparing bvFTD to controls. The paper applies spectral decomposition to produce eigenbrains and conducts group-wise comparisons on eigenvalues and multivariate classification, but it does not provide voxelwise group-level statistical maps or coordinate tables that identify bvFTD-versus-control contrasts in MNI/Talairach space. Therefore inclusion criteria I6 and I7 are not met. No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) are triggered. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

Exclusion E6 applied: the study reports VBM analyses but finds no significant whole-brain (voxelwise) group-level results and instead reports only small-volume (region-of-interest) corrected findings and voxelwise correlations within the patient groups. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (uses VBM), I4 (includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients, n=22), I5 (patient and control group sizes ≥6). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no reported between-group voxelwise contrast comparing bvFTD group directly to controls—analyses focus on correlations within patients and combined patient cohorts rather than bvFTD vs controls), I7 (no significant group-level whole-brain voxelwise result reported for the target group). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study does not meet the requirement for whole-brain, between-group voxelwise results and must be excluded.

Excluded because the study does not provide whole-brain, voxelwise results specific to a bvFTD group (bvFTD subgroup = 5 subjects). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (VBM used), I4 (bvFTD patients were included in the sample), I5 (overall patient group n=15 and control group n=12 meet the >=6 requirement), and I8 (whole-brain results reported in text/figures/supplement). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no between-group contrast reported that compares a bvFTD-only group to controls where bvFTD is not pooled with other FTD subtypes) and I7 (no group-level, whole-brain voxelwise result clearly identified as coming from a bvFTD-only target sample). No exclusion criteria were triggered (none of E5–E9 apply). Because the meta-analysis objective targets bvFTD-specific whole-brain contrasts (unpooled bvFTD group) and this study only reports mixed-FTD contrasts or subgroup analyses where the bvFTD cell has n<6, it does not meet all required inclusion criteria for this review.

This is an empirical study that reports voxel-based morphometry (VBM) whole-brain analyses comparing clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients to healthy controls. The methods state VBM processing in SPM12 with normalization to MNI space and group-level voxelwise t-tests (cluster-based FWE correction) identifying regions of grey matter loss. Sample sizes meet thresholds (12 bvFTD patients, 20 controls). The paper provides whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results attributed to the bvFTD sample (figures and thresholded statistical images). Imaging modality (VBM), diagnostic group (bvFTD), adequate sample sizes, and voxelwise between-group contrasts in a defined stereotactic space are all satisfied. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). No exclusion criteria are met.

This study is excluded because it does not use an eligible imaging modality (I3 not met): it uses structural MRI volumetric/parcellation measures and SuStaIn modeling rather than VBM, task/resting fMRI, or FDG-PET. It also does not report voxelwise, stereotactic (MNI/Talairach) between-group coordinate results or whole-brain voxelwise contrasts (I6 and I7 not met). The analyses are region/cluster-based volumetric comparisons (ROI-style), so exclusion criterion E6 applies. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (bvFTD participants included) and I5 (patient and control group sizes >=6). Inclusion criteria not met: I3, I6, I7. Full text appears complete.

This is a longitudinal structural MRI study of familial FTLD mutation carriers using voxelwise gray matter maps and Bayesian longitudinal modeling; however it does not investigate a clinically diagnosed bvFTD (behavioral-variant FTD) patient group versus controls. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (VBM-style voxelwise structural MRI methods used), I5 (patient group size ≥6: 234 mutation carriers). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (participants are genetic mutation carriers, not a clinically diagnosed bvFTD/Pick's disease patient group), I6 (no reported between-group contrast in MNI/Talairach space comparing a bvFTD patient group to controls), I7 (no group-level, whole-brain voxelwise result clearly reported for a bvFTD patient group). No exclusion criteria from the review were triggered. Therefore the paper does not meet the review’s requirement to include clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients with between-group voxelwise comparisons and must be excluded.

This is a multi-center empirical study that used voxel-based morphometry (VBM) (normalized to MNI space) and reports whole-brain, voxelwise group contrasts (FWE-corrected) comparing bvFTD to controls and to AD. The sample includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (final n=24) and controls (n=37), each >6 participants. The paper presents group-level, whole-brain VBM results (and TBSS DTI results) clearly identified as coming from the bvFTD group. Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6, I7, I8) and no exclusion criteria apply.

This study is excluded because it does not meet imaging-modality and whole-brain voxelwise reporting requirements. Exclusion criteria met: E6 (the imaging analyses are ROI/lobar volumetry rather than whole-brain voxelwise results). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (patient groups exceed 6 participants: C9orf72+ n=23, GRN+ n=10). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (does not use VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET — uses FreeSurfer lobar volumetry and T1-hypointensity/WMSA measures), I4 (participants are genetic mutation carriers in predementia stages, not clinically diagnosed bvFTD/Picks disease patients as required), I6 (no stereotactic MNI/Talairach between-group coordinate results comparing bvFTD to controls), I7 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise results reported). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Given failure to satisfy key inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I6, I7) and presence of ROI-only analyses (E6), the study must be excluded.

This study is excluded because it does not meet the imaging-modality and whole-brain voxelwise reporting requirements. Exclusion criterion met: E6 (reports ROI/volumetric analyses and no whole-brain voxelwise statistical results). Inclusion criteria met: I4 (participants clinically diagnosed with bvFTD), I5 (patient group n≥6 and control group n≥6 for imaging). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (did not use VBM, task/resting fMRI, or FDG-PET; study used structural MRI volumetry/FreeSurfer/BSI and fluid registration), I6 (no between-group contrast reported in MNI/Talairach space with coordinates), I7 (no group-level, whole-brain voxelwise results identified for the target sample). Full text appears complete (contains introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore excluded.

Study uses resting-state fMRI (meets I3), includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (n=42) and healthy controls (n=52) meeting sample-size thresholds (meets I4 and I5). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain parcel-wise comparisons (400-parcel Schaefer atlas) between bvFTD and controls, with mixed-effects models and corrected p-values, presented on standardized cortical surface after normalization to MNI space and in figures/supplementary (meets I6, I7, I8). Analyses are whole-brain (parcel/voxelwise group contrasts) rather than ROI-only or seed-based, and this is an original empirical study. No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) are triggered. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study qualifies for inclusion for the bvFTD imaging meta-analysis.

The study includes a sufficiently sized bvFTD sample (152 patients) and thus meets inclusion criteria I4 and I5. However, it does not use the required imaging modalities (VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET): analyses are surface-based cortical thickness and ROI volumetry derived from FreeSurfer rather than voxel-based morphometry or PET/fMRI (I3 not met). The paper reports ROI- and surface-based regression results, not whole-brain voxelwise group contrasts in a defined stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach) comparing bvFTD to controls, so it fails to meet I6 and I7. Because the study reports only ROI/surface-based cortical thickness analyses and no whole-brain voxelwise results, it violates exclusion criteria E6 and E9. Full text appears complete. Therefore the study must be excluded.

This study includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=19) and control groups (HC n=42, AD n=33), uses resting-state fMRI and whole-brain surface-based morphometry (FreeSurfer) with group comparisons and whole-brain FDR-corrected results, and reports between-group contrasts comparing bvFTD to controls (bvFTD vs HC and bvFTD vs AD). Sample sizes exceed the minimum. Results include whole-brain (voxel/surface-wise) group-level findings attributed to the bvFTD group and seed-based FC associations with AIN connectivity; multimodal neuroimaging and between-group contrasts are clearly described. No exclusion criteria (e.g., review-only, ROI-only, non-empirical, concurrent psychiatric comorbidity) apply based on the full text provided. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Full text is complete. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (VBM used), I4 (clinically diagnosed bvFTD sample), I5 (>=6 patients and >=6 controls), I7 (reports group-level voxelwise (VBM) results from the patient group), I8 (neuroanatomical results summarized in tables/figures). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 — the study does not report a between-group whole-brain contrast comparing bvFTD patients to healthy controls in standard stereotactic space; the imaging analyses are within-patient VBM regressions (correlations with task performance) rather than patient-versus-control voxelwise comparisons. No exclusion criteria from the list apply. Because ALL inclusion criteria must be satisfied and I6 is not met, the study is excluded.

Although this study uses whole-brain VBM in MNI space and includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (n=18) with adequate control numbers, the provided full text does not report any between-group voxelwise contrast directly comparing the bvFTD group to healthy controls in standard space. It does report within-group whole-brain VBM covariate results for bvFTD (VBM correlations with IGT scores) but no explicit bvFTD vs. control voxelwise contrast coordinates/results are presented in the supplied text. Therefore inclusion criterion I6 (at least one between-group contrast comparing bvFTD to controls) is not satisfied. Inclusion criteria met: I3, I4, I5, I7, I8. No exclusion criteria were triggered.

This study meets all required inclusion criteria: it includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (N=13) and healthy controls (N=19) (I4,I5); uses whole-brain VBM structural analyses and resting-state fMRI fALFF (I3); reports group-level, whole-brain between-group contrasts (Ctrl > bvFTD) with results described in MNI space and figures/tables (I6,I7,I8). Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false). No exclusion criteria apply (not a review; not ROI-only; not seed FC/DTI/cortical thickness only; empirical original data).

This study is excluded because it does not meet the key disease-sample and contrast requirements for inclusion. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (voxel-based morphometry was used) and I5 (patient groups, e.g., FTLD n=55, exceed the minimum of 6 participants). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (the sample does not report a clinically diagnosed behavioral variant FTD (bvFTD) or Pick’s disease group specifically — participants are classified by pathological FTLD subtypes rather than a bvFTD clinical subgroup), I6 (no between-group contrast is reported specifically comparing a bvFTD group to controls in MNI/Talairach space — reported contrasts are for FTLD/FTLD subgroups, not bvFTD), and I7 (there is no whole-brain, group-level voxelwise result clearly identified as coming from a bvFTD target sample). Exclusion criteria met: none (no applicable exclusion criteria such as review-only, ROI-only, DTI/FC-only, comorbid sample, or non-empirical). Full text appears complete. Because the review requires results specifically for clinically defined bvFTD (or Pick’s) groups and voxelwise between-group contrasts for that group, this paper cannot be included.

This study uses resting-state fMRI (meets I3), includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients within the sample (7/14; meets I4), has adequate group sizes (FTD n=14, controls n≥6; meets I5), and reports whole-brain voxelwise results with coordinates/figures in MNI space (meets I7 and I8). However, all reported between-group analyses compare the combined FTD-GRN+ group (which mixes bvFTD and avPPA cases) to controls; the paper does not present a bvFTD-only versus controls whole-brain contrast (i.e., the bvFTD group is pooled with other patients). Therefore it fails to meet I6, which requires between-group contrasts where the bvFTD group is not pooled. No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) are triggered. Full text appears complete. Exclusion is based on failure to meet I6.

The full text reports an empirical study including a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (n=27) and healthy controls (n=48). It uses resting-state fMRI (RS fMRI) as an imaging modality (plus TBSS/DTI and cortical thickness). The paper presents group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (TBSS and dual-regression RS-fMRI) with results displayed on the MNI standard brain and describes between-group contrasts (bvFTD vs controls and bvFTD vs EOAD) in standard space. Sample sizes exceed the minimum (≥6). The report contains complete Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion sections. No exclusion criteria apply (not a review, not ROI-only, not non-empirical, no disallowed participant comorbidities, and not limited to seed-based FC/DTI/cortical-thickness-only). Therefore it meets all required inclusion criteria and should be INCLUDED.

This study examines presymptomatic C9ORF72 expansion carriers (preSxC9), not clinically diagnosed bvFTD or Pick's disease patients; therefore it does not meet the core population requirement. Although the paper provides whole-brain VBM and resting-state fMRI voxelwise contrasts comparing preSxC9 to controls, these contrasts are not derived from a bvFTD patient group (so I6 and I7 are not satisfied). It does satisfy I3 (uses VBM and resting-state fMRI), I5 (patient group N=15 and control groups >6), and I8 (reports whole-brain voxelwise results in figures/tables). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete.

The full text is complete. Met inclusion criteria: I3 (uses VBM structural MRI), I4 (includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD group, N=31), I5 (patient and control groups each ≥6; bvFTD N=31, controls N=75). Not met: I6 and I7 — the paper does not report any between-group whole-brain (voxelwise) contrast comparing bvFTD vs healthy controls in standard stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach). The primary VBM results are covariate-only regressions of BIS/BAS scores across the pooled sample and correlations that span diagnostic groups; co-atrophy checks control for diagnosis but no direct group-level bvFTD>control or bvFTD<control voxelwise contrast is presented. No exclusion criteria were triggered (e.g., it is not a review, not ROI-only, not non-empirical). Therefore it fails the requirement for a group-level whole-brain bvFTD vs control result and must be excluded.

This study is excluded because it does not meet the review’s required target diagnosis. Although it uses FDG-PET (I3) and appears to have sufficient group sizes (I5), the patient sample is described as heterogeneous FTLD (frontotemporal lobar degeneration) without specification that participants were clinically diagnosed with behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD) or Pick’s disease. Therefore inclusion criterion I4 is not met. Consequently, the paper does not report whole-brain, group-level voxelwise contrasts specifically comparing a bvFTD (or Pick’s disease) group to controls (I6 and I7 are not satisfied for the target sample). No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) were triggered by the full text. Summary: exclusion IDs met: none; inclusion IDs met: I3, I5; inclusion IDs not met: I4, I6, I7. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical VBM study of bvFTD cases (both C9ORF72 carriers and sporadic bvFTD) including healthy controls. It reports whole-brain voxelwise between-group contrasts (patient groups vs Controls) using MNI space and provides coordinates/figures (including supplementary table). Sample sizes meet the minimum (C9 n=8, sporadic bvFTD n=15, Controls n=15). Whole-brain group-level results for the target bvFTD groups are clearly identified. No exclusion criteria are met. Full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion and imaging details; therefore judged complete.

Although the study uses VBM (I3), includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=28) (I4), and meets sample-size requirements for patients and controls (I5), it does not present any between-group voxelwise contrast comparing the bvFTD group directly to healthy controls in MNI/Talairach space (I6 not met). The VBM results are regression-based across a pooled, mixed-diagnosis sample (polisher/neutral and tarnisher/neutral analyses) and do not report group-level, whole-brain voxelwise results coming specifically from the bvFTD subgroup (I7 not met). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical study that uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) on whole-brain T1-weighted MRI and reports voxelwise group-level contrasts in MNI space. The sample includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD participants (n=26 overall; MRI VBM subset bvFTD n=15) and age-matched controls (MRI controls n=35), meeting sample size requirements. The paper reports between-group voxelwise comparisons (bvFTD vs controls, SD vs controls, and SD vs bvFTD) with cluster-level FDR-corrected results and MNI coordinates. No exclusion criteria apply (not a review, not ROI-only, not only FC/DTI/cortical-thickness, and no evidence of disqualifying comorbid sample). Full text contains introduction, methods (including VBM), results, and discussion and appears complete. Therefore the study meets all required inclusion criteria for the review.

Exclusion criteria met: E6 and E9. This study includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (bvFTD N=10) and healthy controls (N=113) and uses resting-state fMRI (I3, I4, I5 satisfied). However, the analyses are ROI/tract-based (cortical thickness averages, tract-level DWI metrics, and ROI-based functional connectivity) rather than whole-brain, voxelwise mass-univariate analyses reported in stereotactic space. There are no reported group-level, whole-brain voxelwise contrasts with coordinates (MNI/Talairach) for bvFTD vs controls; results are reported as region/tract statistics and boxplots. Therefore the study fails I6 and I7 and meets exclusion E6 (only ROI/tract results, no whole-brain results) and E9 (reports only DTI/tractography, cortical thickness, and seed/ROI-based FC rather than VBM/voxelwise fMRI/FDG-PET).

This study meets the review objective and all required inclusion criteria: it uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) (I3); includes clinically diagnosed behavioural variant FTD subjects (bvFTD) in separate genetic groups (I4); patient groups and controls meet the minimum sample-size threshold (each patient group ≥12 and controls n=40) (I5); reports group-level between-group voxelwise contrasts (VBM) comparing bvFTD groups to controls and between disease groups using SPM with whole-brain results (figures and voxelwise thresholds described) (I6); provides whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results clearly identified for the target groups (I7); and whole-brain results are presented in figures/tables in the text (I8). The full text includes introduction, methods, results and discussion and appears complete. No exclusion criteria are met. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

This is an open-label FDG-PET study in FTD that includes a bvFTD subgroup (n=7) and reports voxelwise, group-level PET results (before vs after memantine) with coordinates. However, it does not include any between-group contrasts comparing a bvFTD group to healthy controls in MNI/Talairach space. The meta-analysis requires at least one between-group contrast of bvFTD versus controls (I6). Therefore the study fails to meet inclusion criterion I6 and must be excluded.

This study uses VBM (I3 satisfied), includes clinically diagnosed behavioural variant FTD participants (bvFTD n=21; I4 satisfied), and meets the sample size requirement (≥6 bvFTD patients; I5 satisfied). However, the paper does not clearly report any between-group, whole-brain voxelwise contrast in a defined stereotaxic space (MNI/Talairach) that compares an isolated bvFTD group (not pooled with other patient groups) to healthy controls in the main text. While the authors state that VBM analyses of FTLD subgroups versus healthy controls are presented in the Supplementary material, the full text does not explicitly present a bvFTD versus control whole-brain coordinate-based contrast clearly attributable to the bvFTD group alone. Therefore inclusion criteria I6 and I7 are not met from the provided full text. No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) apply. Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This study includes a distinct bvFTD group (10 patients) and uses VBM and resting-state fMRI (I3, I4), with adequate sample sizes (controls N=113) (I5). However, the full text reports ROI-based volumetrics, tractography, and ROI-to-ROI functional connectivity and does not present any whole-brain, voxelwise group-level results reported in a standard stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach) as coordinate tables or voxelwise maps for the bvFTD vs control contrast. Therefore it fails to meet I6 and I7. Exclusion criterion E6 (studies reporting only ROI analyses with no whole-brain results) applies. Conclusion: EXCLUDED because E6 is met; inclusion criteria met: I3, I4, I5; inclusion criteria not met: I6, I7.

This multimodal MRI study of MAPT mutation carriers includes resting-state fMRI, DWI, and surface-based cortical thickness analyses, but it does NOT meet key inclusion requirements for a bvFTD coordinate-based meta-analysis. Specifically: (a) I4 not met — participants are genetically defined MAPT mutation carriers stratified by symptom stage; the paper does not report that the patient group is a clinically diagnosed behavioural-variant FTD (bvFTD) cohort (symptomatic carriers can present heterogeneous syndromes and the study does not state that symptomatic subjects are clinically diagnosed bvFTD only). (b) I6 not met — between-group results are reported as surface-based vertex maps and network/tract-level metrics (graph theory and connectome gradients) rather than as between-group voxelwise contrasts with stereotactic MNI/Talairach coordinates required for coordinate-based meta-analysis. The paper does meet I3 (resting-state fMRI included), I5 (sufficient sample sizes across carriers and controls), and I7 (whole-brain vertex-wise cortical thickness results), but failure to meet I4 and I6 precludes inclusion. No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) are triggered. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical VBM study of bvFTD that reports whole-brain voxelwise group contrasts and correlations in standard coordinate space. The paper uses voxel‑based morphometry (VBM) as the imaging modality, includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (N=20 total; N=17 in MRI subset) and healthy controls (N=39 total; N=28 MRI subset), and both patient and control groups exceed the 6‑participant threshold. The authors report VBM atrophy contrasts comparing bvFTD to controls and report voxelwise clusters with coordinates (MNI/Talairach) for both masked reward‑network and whole‑brain analyses. Whole‑brain voxelwise results are clearly described in the text and include coordinate data. Full text contains methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This study is behavioral/olfactory and does not use any neuroimaging modality required by the review (no VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET). Although it includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD patient group (n=45) and control/non-carrier groups (n>=6), it does not report any between-group whole-brain voxelwise contrasts in a standardized stereotaxic space (MNI or Talairach) nor coordinate tables/figures of such results. Therefore it fails key imaging-related inclusion criteria required for the meta-analysis. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical FDG-PET study of clinically diagnosed probable bvFTD patients (n=17) that reports voxel-wise, whole-brain SPM analyses (single-subject comparisons to a normative database and group-level one-sample t-tests) with results presented in SPM/MNI space. Imaging modality = FDG-PET; sample meets size requirement; group-level whole-brain voxelwise results from the bvFTD sample are described and overlaid on an MNI template. No exclusion criteria (e.g., review, ROI-only, non-empirical methods, disallowed modalities, or comorbid psychiatric/neurologic confounds) are met. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore the study meets the review inclusion criteria.

This study is excluded because it does not include clinically diagnosed bvFTD (I4 not met) and it does not report any between-group, whole-brain voxelwise contrasts in a standard space comparing a bvFTD patient group to controls (I6 and I7 not met). It instead studies presymptomatic genetic mutation carriers and uses classification on region-averaged features and TBSS/atlas-based tract averages rather than reporting whole-brain voxelwise group-level results; therefore it meets exclusion criterion E6 (only ROI/tract-summary analyses with no whole-brain voxelwise results). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (resting-state fMRI used) and I5 (sample sizes ≥6). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (no clinically diagnosed bvFTD/picks patients in the target sample), I6 (no reported between-group voxelwise contrasts in MNI/Talairach space for bvFTD vs controls), I7 (no whole-brain group-level voxelwise result from target sample). Full text appears complete.

This study is excluded because it reports only region-of-interest (manual segmentation and shape analysis of caudate and putamen) using structural MRI, with no VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET voxelwise whole-brain analyses. Exclusion criteria met: E6 (ROI-only analyses with no whole-brain results). Inclusion criteria met: I4 (clinically diagnosed bvFTD sample) and I5 (sample sizes: 28 bvFTD, 26 controls). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (imaging modality is structural MRI/manual tracing, not VBM/fMRI/FDG-PET), I6 (no between-group contrast results reported in MNI/Talairach stereotactic coordinates), and I7 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise results). Full text appears complete for screening purposes.

This study is excluded because it reports only ROI-based structural MRI and ASL perfusion analyses rather than VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET voxelwise whole-brain analyses. Exclusion ID met: E6 (only ROI analyses with no whole-brain results). Inclusion IDs met: I4 (includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients) and I5 (patient group N=11 and control group N=20, both ≥6). Inclusion IDs not met: I3 (does not use VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET), I6 (does not report between-group contrasts in standard coordinate space [MNI/Talairach] for voxelwise results), and I7 (does not report group-level whole-brain voxelwise results). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Given these mismatches with the imaging and whole-brain reporting criteria, the study does not meet all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This study uses VBM and includes adequate sample sizes (FTD n=37, controls present), but does not clearly meet key inclusion criteria for this bvFTD-focused review. Specifically, the FTD sample is not clearly described as clinically diagnosed behavioral-variant FTD (only 4/37 explicitly described as behavioural variant), so I4 is not satisfied. The full text does not report any between-group voxelwise contrast coordinates in a defined stereotactic space (MNI or Talairach), nor does it present clearly a group-level whole-brain voxelwise result in stereotactic coordinates; therefore I6 and I7 are not satisfied. No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) are triggered. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (VBM used) and I5 (sample sizes >=6). Inclusion criteria not met: I4, I6, I7. Consequently the study is excluded.

This study is excluded because it does not provide results specific to the target clinical group (bvFTD). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (uses VBM), I5 (patient and control groups exceed 6 subjects), I8 (whole-brain results reported with coordinates/figures). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (does not clearly report that participants are clinically-diagnosed bvFTD specifically; sample is mixed FTD phenotypes), I6 (no between-group contrast presented that compares a bvFTD-only group to controls in stereotactic space). Although whole-brain VBM analyses are reported for FTD and GRN+ vs GRN- comparisons, these are not specific to bvFTD and the bvFTD subgroup is neither isolated nor reported in coordinate-based contrasts. No exclusion criteria from the list (E5-E9) are triggered. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

This study is excluded because it does not meet the imaging-modality and whole-brain stereotactic reporting requirements. It used a linear MRI measure (Bifrontal Index) on structural T1 slices rather than VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET (I3 not met). The sample is diagnosed as FTD using Neary criteria but the paper does not explicitly state behavioral-variant FTD or Pick's disease (I4 not met). No between-group voxelwise contrasts in stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach) or whole-brain voxelwise results are reported (I6 and I7 not met). The study reports only a linear/region-like measure (BFI) rather than whole-brain voxelwise results, which falls under exclusion criterion E6. The study does meet the sample-size requirement (I5: patient group n=23). Inclusion criteria met: I5. Inclusion criteria not met: I3, I4, I6, I7. Exclusion criteria applied: E6. Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false).

The study does not use any of the required imaging modalities (VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET) — it uses visual atrophy scales, cortical thickness measures (CAT12/Desikan atlas), and MRPI derived from structural MRI. While it includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD participants (I4) and adequate sample sizes (I5), it does not report results in a defined stereotactic coordinate space (MNI/Talairach) or provide clearly identified whole-brain voxelwise group-level contrasts required by the review (I6, I7, I8 not met). This study therefore effectively reports regional/atlas-based and visual ROI measures rather than the required voxelwise whole-brain contrasts. Exclusion criteria met: E6 (reports only ROI/region-based analyses with no whole-brain coordinate-based results) and E9 (reports cortical thickness/ROI methods rather than VBM/fMRI/FDG-PET). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical VBM study that includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (n=24) and healthy controls (n=179), both exceeding the minimum sample size. The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise VBM results including between-group contrasts (bvFTD vs controls) with MNI coordinates, and additionally reports whole-brain interaction and region coordinates. Methods, results, and discussion are present and complete. No exclusion criteria apply (not a review, not ROI-only, not non-empirical, not an unsupported imaging modality). Full text appears complete.

Full text is complete. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (uses VBM), I4 (includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients within FTLD sample), I5 (patient group N=37, >6). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no between-group contrast reported comparing a bvFTD group versus healthy controls in MNI/Talairach space—the VBM contrasts compare musicophilic vs non-musicophilic FTLD subgroups, not bvFTD vs controls), I7 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise result clearly identified as coming from a bvFTD-only target sample). Exclusion criteria: none met. Therefore exclude because the study does not provide the required bvFTD-versus-control whole-brain between-group contrasts (I6/I7).

This study meets all inclusion criteria: it uses whole-brain voxel-based morphometry (VBM) (I3); includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (36 bvFTD plus 20 FTD-ALS) (I4); has adequate sample sizes (56 patients, 23 healthy controls) (I5); reports voxel-wise between-group contrasts and VBM analyses performed in MNI space with coordinates provided (including supplementary material) (I6); presents whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results for the target sample (I7); and allows coordinates/results in supplements/figures as acceptable (I8). No exclusion criteria are met: this is an empirical VBM whole-brain study (not a review, ROI-only, DTI/FC-only, or non-empirical), and the sample exclusions (e.g., substance abuse, TBI) were applied by the authors. The full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is a single-family case series with one symptomatic bvFTD proband and some healthy mutation carriers. Imaging includes FDG-PET (so I3 met) and the proband is clinically diagnosed bvFTD (I4 met). However, the study does not meet required sample size (fewer than 6 bvFTD patients; I5 not met), has no control group and reports no between-group voxelwise contrasts in MNI/Talairach space (I6 not met), and provides no group-level whole-brain voxelwise results from a target bvFTD sample (I7 not met). Therefore it fails multiple mandatory inclusion criteria and must be excluded. Full text appears complete.

This study uses VBM and includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (16 bvFTD within 26 FTLD patients) and 21 healthy controls, and the patient and control sample sizes meet minimum thresholds. However the imaging analyses reported are voxelwise regression associations between grey matter and emotion-recognition performance within a combined FTLD cohort (and VBM was performed on FTLD patients only). The paper does not report a between-group voxelwise contrast comparing the bvFTD group (not pooled with other patient groups) to controls in standard stereotactic space, nor does it present bvFTD-specific whole-brain voxelwise results. Therefore it fails inclusion criteria I6 and I7 required by the review. No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) are triggered. Full text appears complete.

This is a longitudinal, empirical study that used voxel-based morphometry (VBM) (SPM2 optimized/modulated VBM) to compare MSTD (Tau +3 intron 10 mutation) patients to age- and gender-matched controls. The VBM analysis included 7 early-stage MSTD patients (all clinically diagnosed with bvFTD) and 19 controls, meeting the sample-size requirement. The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise between-group contrasts with significant clusters and refers to stereotactic locations in supplementary Table 4 (i.e., coordinates in a defined stereotactic space). Whole-brain voxelwise results are clearly identified as coming from the bvFTD-target sample. The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, review/meta-analysis, methods-only, or disallowed imaging modalities) are met.

This is a two-case (n=2) multimodal case-comparison with detailed antemortem/postmortem MRI and histopathology. It does meet I4 (includes a Pick disease [FTLD-tau] patient with bvFTD features). However it does NOT meet key inclusion criteria: I3—imaging modalities are MRI (T1/T2*), not VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET; I5—sample size is only 2 patients (<6 required); I6—no between-group coordinate-based contrasts in MNI/Talairach comparing a bvFTD group to controls (no group analysis); I7—no group-level whole-brain voxelwise results reported for a target patient group. No exclusion criteria from the list were triggered. Full text appears complete. Therefore study must be excluded.

Although the study uses FDG-PET (I3), includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (I4), and has >=6 patients and >=6 controls (I5), it does not provide a group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) contrast that is specific to a bvFTD-only group versus controls. The reported voxelwise maps and group analyses are performed on a mixed FTD patient sample (multiple FTD subtypes pooled), and group-level comparisons are presented mainly as ROI analyses. Therefore inclusion criteria I6 and I7 (bvFTD-only between-group voxelwise contrast and whole-brain group-level voxelwise result from the target sample) are not met. Full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria from the list are triggered.

Exclusion criteria met: E6 and E9. This study reports ROI-based analyses (FreeSurfer cortical/WM ROIs and JHU DTI ROIs) and DTI/cortical-volume measures rather than voxelwise, whole-brain (voxelwise) results in standardized stereotactic space. It does not use VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET as the primary imaging modality. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (clinically diagnosed bvFTD sample, n=14) and I5 (patient group size >=6; AD comparison group n=19). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (study does not use VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET as required), I6 (no between-group contrast reported in MNI/Talairach coordinate space), and I7 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise result reported). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Therefore, exclude per E6 (only ROI analyses/no whole-brain results) and E9 (only DTI/cortical-volume methods rather than required modalities).

This study meets all required inclusion criteria: it uses VBM (voxel-based morphometry) alongside DTI (I3), includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (n=29) (I4), and has an adequate control group (n=37) and patient group sizes (>6) (I5). The paper reports whole-brain, group-level VBM analyses and disease maps for the bvFTD group relative to controls using images in standard MNI space, with results summarized in figures/tables (I6, I7, I8). No exclusion criteria apply: it is an empirical study (not a review), includes whole-brain analyses (not ROI-only), and is not limited to only DTI/seed-based FC/cortical thickness methods. The provided full text is complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion and supplementary references to figures/tables).

The study uses whole-brain VBM and includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (n=20) and healthy controls (n=13), but it does not report any between-group voxelwise contrasts comparing the bvFTD group directly to controls in MNI/Talairach space.
