Therefore it fails inclusion criteria I6 and I7.

This study meets all inclusion criteria for the review objective. It used voxel-based morphometry (VBM) as an imaging modality and explicitly reports VBM analyses (I3). The sample includes a clinically diagnosed behavioural variant FTD (bvFTD) group (n=11) (I4) and includes >=6 participants in the bvFTD group (11) and in controls (8) (I5). The paper reports between-group voxelwise contrasts in a standard stereotactic space (Talairach) comparing diagnostic groups, including bvFTD versus controls, with reported significant clusters and coordinates (I6). It provides whole-brain, group-level voxelwise VBM results clearly identified for the bvFTD group (I7), with results presented in text/tables/figures (I8). Core article content (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion) is present; fulltext_incomplete=false. No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) apply. Therefore INCLUDED.

This is an empirical study with FDG-PET and MRI in a clinically characterized bvFTD cohort, but it does not report any voxelwise/whole-brain (MNI/Talairach) between-group coordinate results. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (FDG-PET used), I4 (includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients), I5 (patient group N=27 ≥6). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no between-group contrast in MNI/Talairach space comparing bvFTD to controls), I7 (no group-level whole-brain/voxelwise results), I8 (no whole-brain results reported as coordinates/figures in standard space). No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) were directly triggered. Therefore exclude because key whole-brain/voxelwise reporting requirements (I6–I8) are not satisfied.

This is an original, empirical study of 30 clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients and 42 healthy controls that (1) used FDG-PET and VBM (voxel-based morphometry) and reported voxelwise, whole-brain group analyses conducted in SPM/MNI space, (2) included adequate sample sizes (patients and controls ≥6), and (3) presented group-level, whole-brain voxelwise results (VBM/DTI analyses) clearly tied to the bvFTD sample. Although the VBM result was null, it is a whole-brain SPM analysis in MNI space; FDG-PET was also performed. No exclusion criteria apply (not a review; not ROI-only; no disallowed exclusive modality). Full text appears complete (intro, methods, results, discussion). Thus the paper meets all inclusion criteria and no exclusion criteria were violated.

The study is excluded because it does not meet the imaging-modality and whole-brain reporting inclusion criteria. Exclusion criteria met: E6 (reports only region-of-interest/lobar SUVR analyses with no whole-brain voxelwise results or coordinate tables). Inclusion criteria met: I4 (includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients, n=9) and I5 (bvFTD group and control group sizes ≥6). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (does not use VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET — uses tau PET and amyloid PET), I6 (no between-group contrast reported in MNI/Talairach space comparing bvFTD to controls), and I7 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise result reported). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This study meets all required inclusion criteria: it uses FDG-PET imaging (I3); includes clinically diagnosed probable bvFTD patients (Rascovsky criteria) (I4) with N=52 (I5); reports voxelwise, whole-brain SPM analyses including a two-sample t-test comparing the bvFTD group (and subgroups) to a normal image database (n=112), i.e., between-group contrasts in stereotactic space (I6, I7). Whole-brain voxelwise results are described (and likely presented as SPM maps/figures), satisfying the acceptable reporting formats (I8). No exclusion criteria apply (e.g., not a review, not ROI-only, not seed-based FC/DTI/cortical-thickness-only, and sample exclusions do not apply). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study meets all inclusion criteria: it uses voxel-based morphometry (SPM-based VBM) and FDG-PET (I3); includes pathologically confirmed Pick disease patients with a bvFTD-presenting subgroup (bvFTD-PiD, n=8) satisfying the target sample requirement (I4, I5) and uses 45 cognitively unimpaired controls (≥6) (I5). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxel-wise SPM comparisons between bvFTD-PiD and controls (FWE/FDR-corrected voxel-wise t tests) and direct between-group contrasts (bvFTD-PiD vs naPPA-PiD) (I6, I7). Results are described in the text and shown in figures (acceptable per I8). No exclusion criteria apply. The full text provided includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false). Therefore the article should be INCLUDED for the meta-analysis.

EXCLUDED: The study uses FDG-PET (I3) and has adequate group sizes (FTLD n=13; controls n=10) meeting I5, but it does not report data specifically from clinically diagnosed behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD) or Pick's disease—patients are described as FTLD without specification of bvFTD (I4 not met). Although voxelwise, whole-brain analyses are reported for FTLD vs controls, the paper does not provide results that can be clearly identified as coming from a bvFTD group, nor does it present between-group contrasts in a defined stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach) for a bvFTD group (I6, I7 not met). Coordinate reporting or bvFTD-specific whole-brain results are not present in the provided full text (I8 not met). No exclusion criteria were triggered (none applicable). Full text appears complete.

The study is excluded because it uses structural MRI morphometry (manual/automated segmentation and radial distance shape mapping of the putamen), not VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET, and reports ROI-based shape/volume analyses rather than whole-brain voxelwise results with stereotactic coordinates. (a) Exclusion criteria met: E6 (reports only ROI analyses with no whole-brain results). (b) Inclusion criteria met: I4 (includes clinically diagnosed behavioral variant FTD patients), I5 (sample sizes: FTD n=33, controls n=17). (c) Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (imaging modality is structural morphometry, not VBM/fMRI/FDG-PET), I6 (no between-group contrasts reported in MNI/Talairach coordinate space), I7 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise results reported). Full text appears complete for assessment.

The study is excluded because it does not meet imaging and whole-brain reporting criteria required for the review. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (participants: clinically diagnosed FTD patients per Neary criteria, with semantic dementia and PNFA excluded, consistent with bvFTD sampling) and I5 (sample sizes: FTD n=44, controls present). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (imaging modality) — the study used structural MRI lobar volumetry and automated regional volumes, not VBM, task/resting fMRI, or FDG-PET; I6 (between-group voxelwise contrasts in MNI/Talairach) — no voxelwise coordinate-based group contrasts are reported; I7 (whole-brain voxelwise group-level result from target sample) — not provided. Exclusion criteria triggered: E6 (reports only ROI/lobar analyses with no whole-brain voxelwise results). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Therefore the paper must be excluded from this meta-analysis.

Exclusion applied: E9 (study reports only cortical thickness methods). Inclusion met: I4 (clinically diagnosed bvFTD sample included), I5 (sufficient sample sizes: 37 bvFTD, 33 controls), I7 (whole-brain vertex-wise cortical thickness analyses performed), I8 (results reported with supplementary material). Inclusion not met: I3 (required imaging modality VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET — this study used structural MRI cortical thickness and subcortical volumetry via FreeSurfer), I6 (unclear/no between-group results reported in a defined stereotactic coordinate space such as MNI/Talairach; vertex-wise surface results do not provide standard voxel coordinates in the paper text). The full text appears complete. Therefore the study must be excluded because it uses cortical thickness methods (excluded by E9) and does not meet the required imaging modalities (I3).

Although the study used FDG-PET (meets I3), it does not provide a group-level, whole-brain between-group contrast specifically for behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD). The FTLD sample is pooled (FTD N=3, SD N=6, mixed N=4) and the paper presents comparisons of FTLD (pooled) and AD versus SCI controls rather than a separate bvFTD (FTD) versus control contrast. The number of bvFTD/FTD cases is only 3 (<6), so the bvFTD patient group does not meet the minimum sample size (I5). Therefore the study fails I4 (target sample not separably reported as bvFTD), I5 (bvFTD group <6), I6 (no bvFTD-vs-control whole-brain contrast where bvFTD are not pooled), and I7 (no whole-brain result clearly identified as coming from a bvFTD target group).

This study meets the review objective and all relevant imaging and sample criteria: (I3) uses Voxel-Based Morphometry (SPM8 VBM) as the imaging modality; (I4) includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=104, with 90 included in VBM analyses); (I5) adequate sample sizes (bvFTD n≈90; controls n=44); (I6) reports between-group VBM contrasts comparing bvFTD subgroups and the bvFTD cohort to age-matched controls (voxelwise T-maps reported and described); (I7) provides whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results (FWE-corrected whole-brain VBM maps); (I8) whole-brain results are presented in figures and described in text (supplementary material referenced). Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion; supplemental materials are acknowledged. No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) are met. Therefore the paper is eligible for inclusion in the meta-analysis of whole-brain imaging in bvFTD.

The study should be excluded because it reports Freesurfer ROI-based structural volume analyses rather than VBM, task/resting fMRI, or FDG-PET, and it does not present whole-brain voxelwise (MNI/Talairach) group-level results. Exclusion criterion met: E6 (ROI-only analyses with no whole-brain results). Inclusion criteria met: I4 (includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients) and I5 (bvFTD group n=48 and controls n=94, both ≥6). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (imaging modality is not VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET), I6 (no between-group contrasts reported in defined stereotactic space), and I7 (no whole-brain voxelwise group-level results). Full text appears complete with methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext_incomplete=false. Given these mismatches with required imaging and whole-brain reporting, the study does not qualify for inclusion in this meta-analysis.

Although the study uses VBM (I3), includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients among its sample (I4), has adequate sample sizes (42 patients, 30 controls; I5), and reports whole-brain VBM results for pathologic groups (so reporting format is acceptable, I8), it does NOT report a between-group contrast that directly compares a clinically defined bvFTD group to controls (in MNI/Talairach space) where the bvFTD group is not pooled with other patient groups (I6). Likewise, it does not provide a whole-brain group-level voxelwise result clearly identified as coming from the bvFTD target sample (I7). No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) are met. Full text appears complete. Therefore the study must be excluded for failing to meet I6 and I7.

This study does not meet the review’s target-sample and whole-brain contrast requirements. It includes FTLD patients (N=31) and uses 18F-FDG PET (I3 satisfied) and has sufficient patient sample size (I5 satisfied). However, it does not specify that the FTLD sample is clinically diagnosed behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD) or Pick’s disease (I4 not met: FTLD is reported generally without bvFTD/Pick’s subgroup breakdown). The paper also does not report any between-group voxelwise contrast in stereotaxic space (MNI/Talairach) comparing a bvFTD group to controls (I6 not met) and therefore provides no group-level, whole-brain voxelwise result clearly identified as coming from a bvFTD target sample (I7 not met). No exclusion criteria from the list (E5–E9) are triggered. Because ALL inclusion criteria must be met and several are not, the study must be excluded.

This is a narrative/book-chapter review (non-empirical) that summarizes prior studies rather than reporting original imaging data or participant analyses. Exclusion criteria met: E8 (non-empirical paper without original data). Inclusion criteria met: none []. Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (no original VBM/fMRI/FDG-PET imaging modality data reported as new analyses), I4 (no original clinically diagnosed bvFTD participant sample reported for primary analyses), I5 (no patient or control group sample sizes reported for original data meeting >=6), I6 (no between-group stereotactic coordinates reported in MNI/Talairach from an original bvFTD vs control contrast), I7 (no group-level, whole-brain voxelwise results from the target sample). Full text appears complete as a review chapter (fulltext_incomplete=false). Therefore the study must be excluded.

Full text is complete. Excluded because it reports manual ROI hypothalamic volume analyses only (no VBM/fMRI/FDG-PET and no whole-brain voxelwise/stereotactic coordinate results). Exclusion criteria met: E6 (ROI-only analyses with no whole-brain results). Inclusion criteria met: I4 (includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD group), I5 (bvFTD n=19 and controls n=23, both ≥6). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (does not use VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET—uses manual hypothalamic tracing on T1 MRI), I6 (no between-group contrasts reported in MNI/Talairach coordinates), I7 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise results). Therefore study is ineligible for the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical VBM study in clinically diagnosed behavioural-variant FTD (bvFTD and bvFTD‑MND). It uses voxel‑based morphometry with registration to MNI152 and reports whole‑brain, voxelwise group contrasts (patients vs controls and direct patient‑group contrasts) with figures/tables and cluster thresholds, and includes coordinate‑based reporting consistent with MNI space. Sample sizes meet thresholds (30 C9orf72+ patients, 30 C9orf72− patients, 30 controls). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8. No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) are triggered. Full text appears complete.

This study meets the review objective and inclusion criteria: it uses FDG-PET (I3), includes clinically diagnosed frontotemporal dementia patients consistent with behavioral-variant FTD (FTD subgroup) (I4), has adequate sample sizes (17 patients, 9 controls) exceeding the minimum of 6 per group (I5), and reports whole-brain, voxelwise SPM group analyses comparing FTD and SD to controls (unpooled FTD vs controls) (I6,I7). The paper presents voxelwise, whole-brain results (BA labels and cluster reporting) and refers to tables/figures for coordinates, which satisfies acceptable reporting formats (I8). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete with methods, results, and discussion provided.

This study used voxel-based morphometry (I3) and included clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (I4) with sufficient sample sizes (22 patients, 22 controls) (I5). It reports between-group voxelwise contrasts aligned to MNI space (I6) and presents results in tables/figures (I8). However, the VBM analysis was performed within a predefined fronto-subcortical region-of-interest mask rather than as an unmasked whole-brain voxelwise analysis. Therefore the paper effectively reports ROI-restricted voxelwise results and does not provide the required group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) result from the target sample, violating the whole-brain evidence requirement (I7). Exclusion criterion E6 (ROI-only analyses with no whole-brain results) is met. Inclusion criteria met: I3, I4, I5, I6, I8. Inclusion criterion not met: I7. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical study that used voxel-based morphometry (VBM) (I3) and reports whole-brain voxelwise group comparisons (FTLD/FTD vs controls) with coordinates in standardized space (MNI) and corrected results, fulfilling whole-brain reporting requirements (I6,I7,I8). The sample includes clinically diagnosed FTD (behavioral variant/frontotemporal dementia) as a distinct subgroup (FTD n=15) within FTLD (I4), with adequate group sizes (FTLD n=25 total; VBM available in 21 FTLD and 17 controls) exceeding the minimum of 6 per group (I5). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, VBM analyses and Discussion, so the full text is complete. No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) are triggered: this is not a review/meta-analysis, not ROI-only, not non-empirical, and it does not use excluded modalities. Therefore the study meets all required inclusion criteria and violates no exclusion criteria.

This study used FDG-PET (I3 satisfied) and included an FTLD patient group of n=11 (I5 satisfied). However it does not report clinically labeled bvFTD/Pick’s disease explicitly (I4 not clearly met), and crucially it does not provide whole-brain, voxelwise group-level results in a standard stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach) comparing bvFTD to healthy controls; results are reported as regional/ROI hypometabolism counts and pattern descriptions rather than voxelwise coordinates (I6 and I7 not met). Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E6 (only ROI/regional analyses without whole-brain voxelwise results). Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This study is excluded because the VBM analyses were constrained to a fronto-striatal ROI mask (region-of-interest voxelwise analysis) rather than reporting whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results. Thus it meets exclusion criterion E6 (ROI-only analyses with no whole-brain results). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (VBM used), I4 (bvFTD sample clinically diagnosed, n=11), I5 (bvFTD n>=6 and controls n>=6), I6 (between-group contrasts reported in stereotactic space comparing bvFTD to controls). Inclusion criteria not met: I7 (does not report at least one whole-brain, voxelwise group-level result for the target sample; analyses were ROI-restricted). Full text appears complete. Therefore the paper must be excluded from the meta-analysis because it provides only ROI-limited voxelwise findings rather than qualifying whole-brain results required by the review.

The study is excluded because it does not use the required imaging modalities nor report whole-brain voxelwise results. Exclusion IDs met: E6 (reports only ROI/aggregate region analyses with no whole-brain voxelwise results) and E9 (uses cortical thickness/volume measures via FreeSurfer rather than VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET). Inclusion IDs met: I4 (clinically diagnosed bvFTD sample) and I5 (patient group sizes ≥6: Part A n=18, Part B n=24). Inclusion IDs not met: I3 (did not use VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET), I6 (no between-group voxelwise contrasts in MNI/Talairach space comparing bvFTD to controls), I7 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise results), and I8 (no whole-brain coordinate tables/figures in defined stereotactic space). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion), so fulltext_incomplete=false. Therefore the paper does not meet all required imaging/whole-brain criteria for inclusion.

The study is a retrospective case series of 8 patients with a clinical diagnosis of FTD and imaging evidence of brain sagging. It meets I3 (FDG-PET/SPECT was performed in 5 patients), I4 (patients were clinically diagnosed with FTD/bvFTD), and I5 (patient group N=8 ≥6). However it does NOT meet I6 (no between-group contrast vs. controls in MNI/Talairach space), and does NOT meet I7 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise statistical results reported/coordinates provided). No exclusion criteria from the review are triggered. Therefore the paper must be excluded because it lacks the required between-group, whole-brain voxelwise comparisons/coordinates required by I6 and I7.

This study reports empirical imaging and behavioral data on clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=14) and age-matched controls (n=19). It includes voxel-based morphometry (VBM) analyses and resting-state fMRI connectivity, reports whole-brain, voxelwise group contrasts and coordinates (e.g., ATL [-45,13,-37]; IFG [-52,2,14]) in standard space, and provides group-level results comparing bvFTD to controls. Sample sizes meet thresholds. Full article text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria (reviews, ROI-only, comorbid psychiatric/other dementia confounds, non-empirical, or limited-to-seed-only methods) apply based on provided content.

This empirical study (Sun et al., 2023) reports task-based fMRI and VBM in a sample of 19 clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients and 20 healthy controls (both >6 participants). Data were normalized to MNI space and the paper reports voxel-wise whole-brain group-level contrasts (faces vs scrambles) with a significant cluster in the left caudate nucleus; searchlight SVM and voxel-wise analyses are reported and described in the text and figures. The study therefore satisfies the meta-analysis inclusion criteria: uses VBM and task-based fMRI (I3), includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD participants (I4), has adequate sample sizes (I5), reports between-group contrasts in stereotactic space (I6), and provides whole-brain, voxelwise group-level results (I7) with acceptable reporting (I8). No exclusion criteria apply (not a review, includes whole-brain results, no disallowed imaging-only methods, and participant sample appears appropriate). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical VBM study that includes a subgroup (ALS-FTD) who met criteria for bvFTD and reports whole-brain voxelwise VBM (SPM/DARTEL) and TBSS results comparing that subgroup to controls; however the patient sample comprises individuals with ALS (a concurrent neurological disorder). This violates exclusion criterion E7 (samples with other neurological symptoms). Therefore the study must be excluded despite meeting the imaging and reporting criteria.

The study is excluded because it does not meet all required inclusion criteria I6 and I7. Met inclusion criteria: I3 (uses fMRI and voxel-based morphometry), I4 (includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients), and I5 (bvFTD group and controls meet minimum n≥6). Not met: I6 and I7 — the voxelwise structural MRI analyses combined bvFTD and PNFA into a single group for patient vs control comparisons, and no group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) contrast exclusively comparing bvFTD to controls in MNI/Talairach space is reported. The fMRI component was performed in healthy young adults only and does not provide bvFTD vs control whole-brain contrasts. No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) were triggered. Full text appears complete.

This is a single-case clinical genetic case report of childhood-onset cerebellar ataxia due to a homozygous SQSTM1 mutation, not a study of behavioral variant frontotemporal dementia (bvFTD). It does not use VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET (violates I3); the sample does not include clinically diagnosed bvFTD/Pick’s disease patients (violates I4); patient group size is N=1, below the required minimum of 6 (violates I5); no between-group contrasts in MNI/Talairach space comparing bvFTD to controls are reported (violates I6); and no whole-brain, voxelwise group-level results from a target bvFTD sample are presented (violates I7/I8). No exclusion criteria from the list are specifically met. Therefore the study does not satisfy the required inclusion criteria for this review and is excluded.

This study is excluded because its neuroimaging methods do not meet the required imaging-modality and whole-brain/voxelwise reporting criteria. Although it includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD sample (N=10) and adequate controls for psychophysiology (meeting I4 and I5), imaging consisted of region-of-interest (FreeSurfer-derived cortical/gray matter volumes) and between-group ROI comparisons (bvFTD vs Alzheimer’s) with no voxelwise VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET analyses and no reported whole-brain coordinate-based (MNI/Talairach) contrasts from the bvFTD group. Thus exclusion criterion E6 (only ROI analyses with no whole-brain results) is met. Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (required imaging modality), I6 (coordinate-based between-group contrasts), and I7 (whole-brain voxelwise group-level results). Full text appears complete for screening (fulltext_incomplete=false).

While the study uses VBM (I3), includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (I4), and has sufficient sample sizes (I5), it does not report a between-group, whole-brain voxelwise contrast comparing a bvFTD group to healthy controls in a defined stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach). The reported whole-brain VBM results are across a heterogeneous patient sample and the bvFTD-specific analyses are ROI-restricted to the insula. Therefore inclusion criteria I6 and I7 are not met. No exclusion criteria from the list apply.

This study meets all inclusion criteria: it uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) as the imaging modality (I3); includes a clinically diagnosed behavioural-variant FTD (bvFTD) group (I4) with N=19 and a healthy control group (N=20), satisfying minimum sample sizes (I5); reports whole-brain, voxelwise between-group and behavioral–VBM analyses with coordinates/cluster reports in standard space (MNI) (I6, I7, I8). It is an empirical original study and does not meet any exclusion criteria (not a review, not ROI-only, not seed-based FC/DTI/cortical-thickness only, and the sample excludes comorbid psychiatric/other dementia cases). The full text provided includes introduction, methods, results and discussion, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This empirical study uses FDG-PET (I3) in a clinically diagnosed bvFTD sample (I4). The final patient group included 21 bvFTD patients and controls (≥6 each; I5). The paper reports voxelwise, whole-brain SPM analyses in standard MNI space with group comparisons (bvFTD vs controls) and regression analyses within the bvFTD group, with coordinates and FWE-corrected results (I6, I7). Results and coordinates are described in the text and figures/supplementary material (I8). No exclusion criteria are met: this is not a review/meta-analysis (not E5), it includes whole-brain results rather than ROI-only analyses (not E6), there is no indication of disqualifying psychiatric comorbidity or substance abuse in the bvFTD sample (E7 not met), it is empirical primary data (not E8), and it does not report only FC, DTI, or cortical thickness (not E9). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

Full text is complete and the study is empirical, uses FDG-PET and includes clinically diagnosed frontal variant/bvFTD patients (n=13) and controls (n=21). It reports whole-brain voxelwise SPM results correlating autobiographical memory measures with resting FDG uptake in the fv-FTD group (i.e., group-level, whole-brain voxelwise results in stereotactic space). However, the paper does not present a between-group voxelwise contrast (bvFTD patients versus controls) reported in MNI/Talairach coordinates. Inclusion criterion I6 (at least one between-group contrast comparing bvFTD to controls in defined stereotactic space) is not met, so the study must be excluded. No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) apply.

This study should be excluded because it fails to meet the minimum sample-size inclusion criterion. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (uses VBM and [18F]FDG-PET imaging modalities), I4 (participants were clinically diagnosed probable bvFTD), I6 (reports between-group voxelwise contrasts in standard space with coordinates/tables), I7 (reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results for the bvFTD group), and I8 (whole-brain results are reported in figures/tables described in text). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (patient group n=5, which is below the required minimum of 6 participants; control group n=10 meets the control requirement). No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) apply. Full text appears complete (contains introduction, methods, results, discussion, and references). Because failure to meet I5 is sufficient for exclusion, the study is excluded.

This study uses voxelwise structural MRI analysis (RAVENS/voxel-based methods) and reports whole-brain voxelwise results, includes clinically diagnosed FTD patients (including behavioral variant cases), and has adequate sample sizes (12 patients, 12 controls). However, the FTD group is pooled across subtypes (behavioral/executive, language variants, corticobasal), and the manuscript does not report any between-group voxelwise contrast specifically isolating a bvFTD (behavioral variant FTD) subgroup versus controls. Therefore it fails Inclusion Criterion I6 (bvFTD group not pooled with other patient groups in reported results). No exclusion criteria from the list are met. Full text appears complete.

This study is excluded because it does not meet key imaging-analysis and sample-type requirements for the meta-analysis. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (FDG‑PET was used), I5 (patient group size = 8 ≥ 6). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (participants are described as FTD but the paper does not explicitly state they are clinically diagnosed behavioral-variant FTD [bvFTD] or Pick’s disease), I6 (no reported between-group voxelwise contrasts in MNI/Talairach space comparing a bvFTD group to controls), I7 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise results or coordinates are reported). Exclusion criteria met: E6 (the paper does not present whole-brain voxelwise results; imaging is used for diagnostic/illustrative purposes rather than reporting voxelwise, coordinate-based group comparisons). Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false). Given the absence of explicit bvFTD sampling and lack of whole-brain voxelwise between-group coordinates/results, the study cannot be included in the coordinate-based meta-analysis.

This is an empirical VBM study that includes a clearly defined bvFTD subgroup (n=64) and compares clinical phenotypes (including bvFTD) to healthy controls (n=32) using whole-brain voxelwise analyses. Imaging modality is VBM (I3). The sample contains clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (I4) and the bvFTD group and controls exceed the 6-participant minimum (I5). The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise group-level results for each phenotype vs controls and specifies statistical thresholds and cluster reporting; results for bvFTD vs controls are described and illustrated (I6, I7). The manuscript references figures and supplementary material for spatial results (acceptable per I8). No exclusion criteria apply. Although coordinate tables are not embedded in the provided excerpt, the methods and references to figures/supplementary materials indicate voxelwise results in a standard space; thus the study meets inclusion criteria for this review.

The study used VBM and resting-state fMRI (I3) and included clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (7 bvFTD cases within the FTD-GRN+ group) (I4). Sample sizes meet minimums (14 patients, control groups ≥6) (I5). The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise group results (VBM and functional maps) (I7) and presents results in figures/tables (I8). However, the critical requirement I6 is not met: the reported between-group contrasts compare a combined FTD-GRN+ group (mixing bvFTD and avPPA) to controls rather than reporting a bvFTD-only versus control whole-brain contrast. The bvFTD subgroup is pooled with other FTD phenotypes in the main analyses, so no bvFTD-specific whole-brain contrast is available. No exclusion criteria were triggered. Therefore the study is excluded for failing inclusion criterion I6.

The study uses task-based fMRI (n-back) and includes 7 FTD patients, and reports whole-brain, voxelwise group results with Talairach coordinates (supplementary tables). However, it does not explicitly state that the patient sample is behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD) or Pick’s disease (I4 not clearly met). Also, the between-group contrasts reported compare FTD to Alzheimer’s disease patients rather than to healthy controls; inclusion criterion I6 requires a between-group contrast comparing bvFTD to controls. Therefore not all required inclusion criteria are satisfied. No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

Although this empirical paper uses VBM (I3) and includes a clinically diagnosed frontal variant FTD subgroup (behavioral variant FTLD/FTD) with n=14 and a control group with n=20 (I4, I5 satisfied), it does not report a whole-brain, group-level voxelwise between-group contrast in MNI/Talairach space that isolates the bvFTD (FTD) group versus controls. The VBM analyses reported are correlational (brain volume correlated with antisaccade performance) and, importantly, the primary VBM models controlled for or used a combined FTLD group (FTD+SD+PA) rather than presenting a direct bvFTD (FTD) >/< control voxelwise contrast. Therefore the study fails to meet I6 and I7 (no bvFTD-specific whole-brain between-group voxelwise results). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Inclusion criteria met: I3, I4, I5. Inclusion criteria not met: I6, I7. Exclusion criteria met: none.

The study is excluded because it reports only ROI/parcellation-based metabolic connectivity analyses (60 AAL VOIs) and does not present any whole-brain, voxelwise, coordinate-based (MNI/Talairach) between-group contrasts for behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD) versus controls. Study uses VBM and includes a clinically defined FTD (bvFTD) subgroup (n=47) and healthy controls (n=43), meeting imaging and sample-size criteria. Therefore it fails to meet I6 and I7 (bvFTD-specific between-group, whole-brain results). No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) apply. Excluded on the basis of missing bvFTD-specific whole-brain between-group results.

This study uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) (I3) and includes a clinically diagnosed frontal-variant FTD group (FTD-fv, equivalent to bvFTD) (I4). No exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical study that used voxel-based morphometry (VBM) whole-brain analyses to examine neural correlates of empathy in clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients. Therefore the study meets all required inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6, I7, I8) and is suitable for inclusion in the meta-analysis focused on bvFTD VBM studies.

This full-text reports whole-brain voxel-based morphometry (VBM) analyses (SPM12/DARTEL) relating grey-matter intensity to memory measures and presents group-level, voxelwise results corrected in MNI space. This study is excluded because it does not meet key inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis. Although it includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD sample (n=11) and reports whole-brain voxel-wise TBM results (including voxel-wise regressions within the bvFTD group), the imaging modality used is tensor-based morphometry (TBM), not one of the required modalities (VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET) (I3 not met). In addition, the primary between-group contrasts reported compare bvFTD to early-onset Alzheimer’s disease (AD), not to healthy control subjects as required by the criterion specifying a between-group contrast versus controls in standard stereotaxic space (I6 not met). Therefore, despite meeting I4 (bvFTD sample), I5 (sufficient patient group size), and I7 (reports whole-brain voxelwise group-level results from the target sample), failure to satisfy I3 and I6 prevents inclusion in this meta-analysis. Full text appears complete.

This study meets the review objective and all required inclusion criteria. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an original empirical study of clinically diagnosed bvFTD (N=63) using voxel-based morphometry/voxelwise grey-matter analyses (ANTs preprocessing, FSL randomise) comparing bvFTD to healthy controls (N=55). Full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion and appears complete.

This is an original empirical neuroimaging study of clinically diagnosed probable bvFTD patients (Rascovsky criteria). It used voxel-based morphometry (VBM) on MRI and FDG-PET with voxelwise SPM5 analyses and partial-volume correction, reporting group-level whole-brain voxelwise between-group contrasts (patients vs. controls) with tables/figures in stereotactic space. No exclusion criteria were met (not a review, not ROI-only, no comorbid psychiatric/substance cases, not non-empirical, and not only seed-based FC/DTI/cortical thickness). Therefore the paper meets all required inclusion criteria and should be INCLUDED.

The study reports whole-brain, voxelwise FDG-PET SPM analyses comparing FTD groups to controls and has adequate sample sizes (FTD n=29; controls n=11; FTD/MND n=8). Inclusion criterion I4 (explicit bvFTD or Pick's disease sample) is therefore not met, and I6 (a between-group contrast explicitly of bvFTD versus controls) cannot be confirmed. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Inclusion criteria met: I3, I5, I7, I8. Inclusion criteria not met: I4, I6. No exclusion criteria from the provided list are triggered.

This is a VBM study of clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients with autopsy-confirmed diagnoses and voxel-wise whole-brain analyses. Sample size for patients with imaging (n=82) exceeds the minimum (≥6). The methods explicitly describe voxel-wise, whole-brain analyses in standard space and comparisons to control data to generate W-scores. Although coordinate tables are not shown in the extracted text, whole-brain voxelwise group results are clearly reported in figures and described in the text, satisfying the requirement for whole-brain, group-level results for the bvFTD group. Full text appears complete.

Full-text screening summary: No exclusion criteria met. This study is an ROI manual volumetry study of the putamen using structural T1 MRI, not VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET; it does not report any whole-brain, voxelwise results or coordinates (MNI/Talairach). This empirical study used voxel-based morphometry (VBM) and explicitly included a behavioral variant FTD (bvFTD) cohort (n=10) alongside healthy controls (n=10). This full text reports whole-brain voxel-based morphometry (VBM) analyses (FSL-VBM) and provides group-level, voxelwise contrasts comparing patient groups to healthy controls with MNI coordinates and figures/tables. This study uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) (I3) and includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (21 bvFTD patients) and healthy controls (46), meeting sample-size requirements (I4, I5). Therefore inclusion criteria I6 and I7 are not satisfied. Full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) are met. Excluded because the paper does not report a between-group voxelwise contrast comparing the bvFTD group to healthy controls in a defined stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach). This study performs voxel-based morphometry (VBM) analyses on a bvFTD subgroup (N=12) with comparison to healthy controls (12 for VBM; NC behavioral group N=16), reports whole-brain, voxelwise two-sample t-test contrasts and regression analyses relating IRI empathy scores to gray-matter atrophy using standardized coordinate space (SPM normalization to template), and presents voxelwise results (clusters reported and tabulated). This full-text reports an empirical voxel-based morphometry (VBM) study (FSL VBM) examining dementia groups including a clearly defined behavioural-variant FTD (bvFTD) subgroup (n=11).
